BiblicalUsage: The word means to refuse, to be unwilling, and it is the word of Pharaoh's stubbornness. If you refuse to let my people go, God says, I will smite your borders with frogs, and if you refuse and hold them still, the plagues will follow, and if you refuse again, the locusts will come tomorrow. Jeremiah hears the same word when he tells Zedekiah that if he refuses to go forth to the king of Babylon, the city will fall.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe refusal is the sin that hardens with every warning, because each no makes the next one easier. I hold that Pharaoh's refusals built his own ruin, and the same word still stands before every heart that will not let God's people go.
